findings.title: Possible NPE when the Clients type resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission(client, scope), when the per-client resource is null, getResourceTypeResource(...) is called. It can return null (for example when authz schema support is off, or the resource was not created). The result is passed straight to findByResource(server, resource) and later to resource.getScopes(), so a null causes a NullPointerException instead of returning false. Add a null check.

findings.title: Fallback to all-clients can grant permission when the per-client resource exists
findings.body: If a client-specific resource exists, evaluation uses only that resource. The evaluation of a specific resource with permissions defined only on the type resource may therefore not fall back to the all-clients permission. In addition, when no specific resource exists, the all-clients resource is evaluated with all of its scopes, which is okay. The two paths are inconsistent and the first path can deny access that the all-clients permission should grant.

findings.title: canMapRoles/composite/clientScope ignore all-clients permission
findings.body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission(client, ...). The Javadoc in ClientPermissionEvaluator says the all-clients scope also applies, but the resource type path is used only when no per-client resource exists. A client with its own resource therefore loses the all-clients grant. The check for CONFIGURE also does not imply MANAGE semantics consistently.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports
findings.body: The private getEvaluationContext method, the logger, the TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import, and the Scope import are all unused. This is dead code that should be removed.

findings.title: Role/client/group removal listener gated on feature flag changes behavior
findings.body: The listener body is now wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ). This is an unrelated behavior change, and it is also a risk: with V2 enabled and the V1 feature off, no cleanup runs. Meanwhile ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so if both are enabled, deleting a client or role would throw from the listener. The change is neither described nor tested.
